Date: July 1, 2024

Goal of this file is to test adding color coding to excel files

```{r}
rm(list=ls())

library(openxlsx)
library(here)

# Create a sample dataframe
df <- data.frame(
  ID = 1:5,
  Fruit = c("apple", "banana", "cherry", "banana", "apple"),
  Fruit2 = c("apple", "banana", "cherry", "banana", "apple"),
  Quantity = c(10, 20, 15, 5, 8)
)

# Create a new workbook and add a worksheet
wb <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb, "Sheet1")
addWorksheet(wb, "Sheet2")


# Write the dataframe to the worksheet
writeData(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", x = df)

# Create styles for highlighting
appleStyle <- createStyle(fontColour = "#FFFFFF", bgFill = "#FF0000") # Red background, white text
bananaStyle <- createStyle(fontColour = "#000000", bgFill = "#FFFF00") # Yellow background, black text

# Apply conditional formatting for "apple"
conditionalFormatting(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", cols = 2, rows = 2:(nrow(df) + 1), rule = '=="apple"', style = appleStyle)

# Apply conditional formatting for "banana"
conditionalFormatting(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", cols = 2, rows = 2:(nrow(df) + 1), rule = '=="banana"', style = bananaStyle)

# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, file = "highlighted_fruits.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

```


Now let's try again but use some better targeting of the columns. I want to target all the columns that start with Fruit.

```{r}
# Write this conditional formatting again, except make it more robust so that if the fruit field is no longer the second column, it will still work.

# Create a new workbook and add a worksheet
wb <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb, "Sheet1")

# Write the dataframe to the worksheet
writeData(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", x = df)

# Create styles for highlighting
appleStyle <- createStyle(fontColour = "#FFFFFF", bgFill = "#FF0000") # Red background, white text
bananaStyle <- createStyle(fontColour = "#000000", bgFill = "#FFFF00") # Yellow background, black text

# Get the column indices for all columns beginning with "Fruit"
fruit_col <- which(grepl("^Fruit", colnames(df)))
# fruit_col <- which(colnames(df) == "Fruit")

# Apply conditional formatting for "apple"
conditionalFormatting(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", cols = fruit_col, rows = 2:(nrow(df) + 1), rule = '=="apple"', style = appleStyle)

# Apply conditional formatting for "banana"
conditionalFormatting(wb, sheet = "Sheet1", cols = fruit_col, rows = 2:(nrow(df) + 1), rule = '=="banana"', style = bananaStyle)

# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, file = "highlighted_fruits_v2.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```
